summary: The study investigates the impact of Germanium surface conditioning and ALD-growth temperature on Al2O3/ZrO2 high-k dielectric stacks. It demonstrates that deposition on germanium-oxide-free substrates using HBr-etching pretreatment yields higher breakdown voltages. Lower deposition temperatures (150°C) result in decreased leakage currents and lower inversion capacitances at high frequencies. The process involves ALD using TMA and tetrakis(diethylamino)zirconium precursors with H2O as the oxygen source.

Metal-carrying precursors are trimethylaluminum (TMA) for the Al2O3 deposition and chlorine-free tetrakis(diethylamino)zirconium for the ZrO2 deposition, which is at least stable up to 350°C.
